about_blocks.text: About Envision Mind Care in Edmonton

Envision Mind Care & Research Institute is a private mental health and addiction clinic at 9807 106 Street NW in downtown Edmonton, a short walk from the Alberta Legislature. Most of its work is outpatient: psychiatry, psychology, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), family medicine and physiotherapy, for adults dealing with depression, anxiety, OCD, ADHD, trauma, chronic pain and substance use.
about_blocks.html: Envision Mind Care & Research Institute is a private mental health and addiction clinic at 9807 106 Street NW in downtown Edmonton, a short walk from the Alberta Legislature. Most of its work is outpatient: psychiatry, psychology, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), family medicine and physiotherapy, for adults dealing with depression, anxiety, OCD, ADHD, trauma, chronic pain and substance use.

about_blocks.text: For addiction, the clinic runs a substance use disorder program in two formats. The outpatient version runs Monday to Friday at the clinic while you live at home. The in-patient version is six weeks, with longer stays if the team thinks you need them, and you sleep in a private bedroom at the same downtown building. The clinic says both programs run at this address. Envision Mind Care appears on the Government of Alberta's list of licensed residential addiction treatment service providers under the Mental Health Services Protection Act.

about_blocks.text: The program is non-12-step and trauma-informed. It starts with assessments by addiction specialists, psychologists and psychiatrists, then mixes regular psychiatric reviews, one-to-one addiction counselling, group sessions using CBT, DBT and motivational interviewing, substance use education workshops and yoga. TMS can be added to target cravings and low mood, and medication-assisted treatment is used where it fits. In-patient clients also see a dietitian.

about_blocks.text: Envision has treated more than 300 people with TMS, about 15,000 sessions in all, on MagVenture and BrainsWay machines. It also offers psychedelic-assisted treatment in specific cases where standard care has not worked. The clinic says it was the first in Alberta licensed for psychedelic drug treatment services under the MHSPA, from August 19, 2024, and that the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta has accredited it for psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy.

about_blocks.text: You do not need a doctor's referral; the clinic takes self-referrals by phone or form. Substance use treatment is mostly private pay, with payment plans available. The clinic says veterans, teachers and first responders on disability can often use their benefits to cover care, and people on WCB can ask about the program. Psychology sessions follow the Psychologists' Association of Alberta fee guide and can be direct billed to several insurers.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Envision Mind Care

faqs.question: Is Envision Mind Care an inpatient or outpatient rehab?

answer_blocks.text: Both, though most of what the clinic does is outpatient. Its substance use disorder program has an outpatient version, Monday to Friday while you live at home, and a six-week in-patient version where you stay in a private bedroom at the clinic. Envision is listed by the Government of Alberta as a licensed residential addiction treatment service provider.

faqs.question: How long is the in-patient program?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic says the in-patient substance use program is six weeks, with the option to stay longer based on clinical assessment. Its program summary describes four to six weeks plus follow-up sessions. The outpatient substance use program runs about three to six weeks, also with follow-up.

faqs.question: What does a day in the outpatient program look like?

answer_blocks.text: The outpatient program runs five days a week, with sessions between 8:15 am and 5:00 pm and the odd appointment outside those hours, including Saturdays. It covers psychiatry visits, TMS, weekly one-to-one addiction counselling, substance use education workshops, psychology group sessions and yoga. The clinic keeps groups small.

faqs.question: What is TMS and how is it used for addiction?

answer_blocks.text: Transcranial magnetic stimulation uses magnetic pulses through a coil on the scalp to stimulate parts of the brain. Health Canada has approved it for depression that has not responded to other treatment. Envision adds TMS sessions to some substance use plans, saying it may help reduce cravings and withdrawal and lift mood alongside counselling.

faqs.question: Does Envision Mind Care offer ketamine or psychedelic therapy?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic's site mentions ketamine therapy and has a page on psychedelic-assisted treatments. It says these are not first-line care and are only considered after a full medical and psychiatric assessment, when standard treatment has not worked, and under physician supervision. Envision says it holds an Alberta psychedelic drug treatment services licence and CPSA accreditation for psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy.

Veterans, teachers and first responders on disability may be able to use their benefits, and psychology sessions can be direct billed to several insurers.

faqs.question: Does Envision Mind Care offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic does not describe a stand-alone medical detox unit, and its recovery.com profile lists detox as not offered. faqs.question: Can people from outside Edmonton or Alberta attend?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. The clinic says out-of-province clients can use its programs and that people come from across Canada and abroad. The in-patient option suits people from places like Fort McMurray, Grande Prairie or Red Deer who cannot travel into Edmonton every day.
